title: The Photo Booth
hook: The arcade owner had one rule: once the boardwalk lights go out, never sit in the photo booth.
lines: The old arcade on the boardwalk has a photo booth in the back corner.
The owner had one rule for whoever closes up: once the boardwalk lights go out, never sit in that booth.
Then, on the last night of the season, the lights went dark... and behind me, the booth started up on its own.
Nobody was inside. But the curtain was swaying, like someone had just stood up.
A strip of photos dropped into the tray.
Three pictures of the empty seat... and in each one, the curtain was pulled open a little wider.
In the last one, a pale hand was holding it open.
I left the keys on the counter and walked home without looking back.
It wasn't until I got into bed that I remembered... that booth always prints four pictures.
This morning, the fourth one was on my pillow.
It was me, asleep... taken from right beside my bed.
